title: Result of a galactic crash
caption: The galaxy NGC 4490, the Cocoon Galaxy, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4490 · constellation Canes Venatici · about 25 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA Acknowledgements: D. Calzetti (UMass) and the LEGUS Team, J. Maund (University of Sheffield), and R. Chandar (University of Toledo)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows the galaxy NGC 4490, whose shape looks scattered and warped rather than neatly organised. That disorder is the aftermath of a collision with another galaxy, NGC 4485, which lies outside this frame.

Galaxies that pass close to each other pull on one another with tidal forces, gravity that tugs harder on the near side than the far side. In this case those forces were extreme. They sculpted both the shape of NGC 4490 and its properties, and they stretched its outer regions out into long extensions.

NGC 4490 was once a barred spiral galaxy, a spiral with a straight bar of stars across its middle. The stretching of its outskirts earned it the nickname the Cocoon Galaxy. Its listed type is a starburst galaxy, one forming stars at a high rate, which fits the picture of a galaxy stirred up by a close encounter.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.73 x 2.62 arcminutes) and distance (25 million light years), the frame spans roughly 20,000 × 19,000 light-years. Its light set out about 25 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters from the ultraviolet through visible light, including one that isolates the glow of hydrogen. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet part of this data is invisible to the human eye, and the galaxy itself is far too faint to see this way without a telescope.
